title: The FBI Got Hacked. Here's What That Actually Means
partialText: Chinese state-sponsored actors breached the FBI's surveillance coordination systems — not to steal data, but to see who the Bureau was watching. The "Major Incident" designation triggered a whole-of-government response, and the architectural lessons apply far beyond government networks.

title: 25 Things the Claude Code Leak Reveals About Anthropic’s AI Agents
partialText: A temporary npm release exposed Claude Code’s internals, revealing key design decisions around memory, orchestration, tooling, and safety.

title: Break the Loop, Part 2: From Data Structures to Computational Control
partialText: In this part, we transition from data structures to the "physics" of functions. We'll cover why currying is the default, how tail recursion saves your memory, and how to build a Monad from scratch to handle empty results gracefully.

title: Stateless AI Agents Are the Real Problem
partialText:
AI agents don’t actually learn from experience, they reset after every run.
Chat history is not real memory and doesn’t scale well.
Without memory, agents keep repeating the same mistakes and rediscovering solutions.
A simple memory layer can store facts, past events, and learned steps.
Even basic memory makes agents more consistent and efficient over time.
You don’t need complex systems, just enough memory to retain what worked and what didn’t.

title: Principal Components in TypeScript (Part 2): How PCA Actually Works Under the Hood
partialText: This piece walks through PCA step by step—centering data, building covariance matrices, applying SVD, and using eigenvectors to compress and analyze data.

title: Grant Cardone Is Challenging REITs With a Bitcoin–Real Estate Hybrid. Will It Work?
partialText: Grant Cardone is building a real estate Bitcoin hybrid company. The company buys commercial real estate below replacement cost. The spread between what they pay and what the property is worth gets stacked in Bitcoin.

title: Where Is Africa in Jensen Huang’s Five-Layer AI Cake?
partialText:
Africa isn’t one country, but it shares the same structural gaps: energy, water, education.
Ethiopia shows what’s possible with sovereign energy investment.

Jensen Huang’s five-layer AI model highlights a hard truth: Africa mostly consumes, it doesn’t build.
China proves energy is the real competitive edge.
No energy, no development. No development, no tech. No tech, no AI.

The path forward is simple: build power, cut bureaucracy, get pragmatic or stay behind.

title: How Retail Coupon Data Changed the Way I Think About Growth Systems
partialText: Growth systems plateau when built on segments and averages. Moving to real-time, probability-based decisions improves performance and ROI.

title: How I Decide Whether Module Federation Is Worth It
partialText: Module Federation enables cross-framework UI sharing, but adds complexity. Use it only when reuse and independent scaling outweigh the costs.

title: How Persistent Prompt Injection Attacks Live On After You've Locked the Door
partialText: Prompt injection isn’t just session-based. Persistent attacks embed in data and survive access revocation, requiring new AI security architectures.

title: Between Scalpel and Infinity
partialText: A man facing surgery becomes convinced he will die, but instead experiences a surreal detachment from his body under anesthesia. His consciousness drifts into space, observing Earth and the cosmos with cold clarity. As time and perception distort, he confronts existence itself—only to awaken and realize he survived, forever changed by the experience.

title: The Internet’s Next Premium Feature May Be Human Verification
partialText: As automation scales, trust becomes scarce. Human verification is emerging as a premium layer that restores authenticity and value online.

title: The Price of Borrowed Life
partialText: A struggling medical student is chosen as heir by a mysterious old philosopher, only to awaken in the man’s aging body after a strange drink. Realizing his youth has been stolen through a sinister consciousness transfer, he is trapped, dismissed as insane, and left powerless. Meanwhile, the old man begins life anew in his body—revealing a terrifying path to immortality.

title: Jungle That Guards Its Gold
partialText: Two exhausted treasure hunters locate hidden gold on a remote island using a worn map. Near the site, they discover a dead man and overlook subtle warning symbols. While handling the treasure, both are pricked by poisoned thorns—an intentional trap set to protect the hoard. As paralysis sets in, they realize too late that the treasure was designed to kill anyone who found it.

title: AI’s Critical Role in Healthcare and Online Safety
partialText: AI is no longer optional in high-stakes systems like healthcare and online safety. From real-time medical documentation to detecting child exploitation at global scale, automation fills the gap human teams cannot handle. While AI introduces new risks, it also provides the strongest defense—making “safety by design” and large-scale deployment essential for protecting vulnerable populations.

title: A New York Times Investigation Named Its Satoshi
partialText: A New York Times investigation by John Carreyrou identified Adam Back as Satoshi Nakamoto, but just 11 days later, the documentary Finding Satoshi presents a competing conclusion. Built on four years of research, expert interviews, and behavioral analysis, the film reframes Bitcoin’s origins through the lens of cypherpunk ideology rather than a single individual.

title: How Zodia Custody's BitMEX Integration Quietly Rewires Institutional Crypto Market Structure
partialText: BitMEX, the exchange that invented the perpetual swap, is now live on Zodia Custody's Interchange off-venue settlement network. Clients trade on BitMEX while assets stay in bank-grade cold storage until settlement. After FTX's $12.7B judgment and Bybit's $1.5B hack, the move is less a product launch and more a structural signal that execution and custody have decoupled in institutional crypto.

title: The Volunteer DDoS: Why AI Security Tools Are Breaking the Infrastructure They're Meant to Protect
partialText: AI security tools are creating more work for open source maintainers, not less. Claude Mythos just raised the stakes. The governance fix already exists.

title: From Broken Token Models to Market-Driven Governance: Interview with Umia CEO Francesco Mosterts
partialText: Crypto spent the last decade making assets programmable. Moving forward, next phase need to be making organizations programmable.

title: ML Internals: The Week I Stopped Treating Embeddings as a Black Box
partialText: A hands-on dive into embeddings, tokenization, and why the model is just one piece of an ML system.
